bill.title: Supporting the recognition of September 16, 2025, as "National Voter Registration Day".
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
bill.officialSummary: This resolution supports the designation of National Voter Registration Day and encourages those eligible to vote to register, confirm their personal information on record with election officials, and vote.

classification.plainSummary: This resolution expresses support for designating September 16, 2025, as National Voter Registration Day. It encourages eligible citizens to register to vote, verify their registration information with election officials, and participate in elections. As a symbolic resolution, it does not create new law or change existing policy.

plain.whatItDoes: This resolution would support the designation of National Voter Registration Day and encourage those eligible to vote to register, confirm their personal information on record with election officials, and vote.
plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who deals with a federal agency.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in dealing with the government. Nothing has changed yet. This kind of resolution does not become law, even if it passes.
plain.source: Reworded from the official summary. Staff at the Congressional Research Service wrote that summary. It is public domain, and the full text of it is further down this page.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
